tagline: The old Westport pike, into Louisville along the Ohio.
intro: River Road begins at US 42 near Prospect and runs seven miles southwest beside the Ohio into Louisville, ending at Zorn Avenue. It was built as the Louisville-Westport Pike.

The railroad came out this way in the 1870s, the Louisville, Harrods Creek and Westport, and never reached Westport. Prospect grew up around one of its stations, named either for the view from the hill or for the expected completion of the line, which went bankrupt in 1879. Louisville families followed the tracks out to build country estates.

moments.title: Harrods Creek
moments.text: Harrod's Tavern was an early stopping point for boats headed downstream, and the building lives on, heavily rebuilt, as the Captain's Quarters bar and restaurant.

moments.title: Glenview
moments.text: Old estate houses stand on high bluffs over the Ohio here, and when Louisville tried to annex the place in 1983 its residents had it made a city of its own.

moments.title: Louisville Water Tower
moments.text: At the end of the byway a 183-foot Doric column rises from a Corinthian portico, built handsome so a skeptical city would warm to the water company that started pumping here in 1860.

sources.label: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Kentucky State and National Scenic Byways and Highways
